analysis.title: Higher Floor, No Fuel: Why McElligott Thinks Vol Stays Elevated But Can't Explode
key_insights: Nomura's McElligott says the VIX floor has moved up from 15-16 to 18 and the VVIX floor from the 80s-90s to the mid-90s, after realized vol of VVIX hit a 10-year record above COVID, Liberation Day and Volmageddon. He expects a higher realized vol world until a few 'spinning plates' clear, possibly after the Anthropic (ANT) IPO is completed and supply digested.

McElligott sees no conditions for a vol squeeze ('No Juice to Squeeze') because the VIX complex lacks negative gamma, real or synthetic. Leveraged VIX ETNs have been purged to barely net long, and VIX options dealers are long gamma.

Nomura data: VIX ETN vega flows negative four straight weeks, -$20.2M week-to-date (6th percentile). Create/redeem flows were -$11.7M in the week of Nov 6 and -$33.7M over the past month (4th percentile), about $35M of vega out in four weeks. Korean retail, the largest source of leveraged VIX ETN demand, redeemed into last week's equity smash.

VIX options dealers' total gamma out to six months is +1.8M (91st percentile). Customer demand for VIX calls is low and deep OTM. Long-gamma dealers sell vol when it rises and buy when it falls, the opposite of what feeds a squeeze.

Nomura estimates a 10-point vol jump would force only $26M of vega buying across VIX ETNs and VIX options (5th percentile since 2019, vs peaks near $150M in 2019 and mid-2024). A 30-point shock would force $104M (21st percentile).

Spot-vol correlation is returning to the traditional negative relationship. Month-to-date S&P realizes 22.9 vol on up days vs 41.8 on down days (ratio about 0.5, 4.5th percentile since 1986). Nasdaq 100 realizes 30.5 vs 62.8 (2.2nd percentile in 40 years).

McElligott says the one mega flow that can offset negative spot-vol is exotic/structured-note issuance, where dealers must buy vol as spot rises and sell vol as spot falls. Approximate Nomura chart reads: about $130M vega per vol point to buy on +10%, about $340M at +30%, over $500M at +50%. Dealers supply vol peaking near $240M per vol point around a 25% drop.

Goldman's derivatives desk likes owning downside skew (S&P December 7300/7850 risk reversal), reasoning the street is structurally short vol on the way down and long vol on the way up. This contrasts with McElligott's exotics chart. Goldman's S&P implied move through Friday was 1.10%, which the index covered by Wednesday lunch.

McElligott says vol can rise in both directions ('Up Vol is Still Vol Too') because the straddle and price distribution are wider and nobody has any 'Net On'. With Nasdaq futures up 2.9%, QQQ fixed-strike vols were higher across nearly every expiry from Nov 20 out, deep OTM puts were bid along the curve, and S&P fixed-strike vol was about to turn higher.

Nomura's live estimate of levered ETF end-of-day buying is +$26.5B (3.8-sigma), 1.22% of full-day volume and 15.4% of last-hour volume. Semis are $14.9B (56%), Mag7 $3.8B, Info Tech $3.6B. Semis and Tech are 100th percentile, total is 99th. It compares with +$34.3B on the April 2025 tariff pause day and last Thursday's -$48.6B dump.

Levered ETF complex AUM is $151.5B (from $142B the day before) with about $7.6B to trade per 1% move (from $6.5B). Creations hit 100th percentile after the crash. The complex is 86% AI-centric as of last week.

Goldman desk data: Vol of Vol had its 2nd largest one-day increase on record last Thursday and a top-10 one-day decline Monday. Panic Index is 6.5/10, last Thursday was the largest put volume session ever, and US net leverage is at 5-year lows on Goldman's Prime book.

Zero Hedge's own view: with ETN buyers gone and dealers long gamma, the next selloff may show a large S&P drop without a VIX spike. Forced buyers of vol are gone, but forced buyers and sellers of stocks are larger than ever.

tension_points.bull_case: Nomura: VIX complex has no negative gamma. ETNs are purged and VIX dealers are long gamma, so a 10-point vol jump forces only $26M of vega buying.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman likes owning downside skew because the street is short vol on the way down. Zero Hedge notes forced stock buyers and sellers are bigger than ever, so a large spot drop may occur without a VIX spike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Nasdaq 5% daily move showing which book (Goldman's index flow or Nomura's exotics flow) is larger.

tension_points.bull_case: Traditional negative spot-vol has returned, with down days about twice as volatile as up days.
tension_points.bear_case: Exotics hedging flows (dealers buy vol as spot rises, sell as it falls) offset the return to normal spot-vol behavior.

theme_stances.key_argument: VIX floor moves to 18 on regime shift, but a purged ETN base and long-gamma VIX dealers leave no squeeze fuel.
Levered ETFs must buy about $26.5B into the close, concentrated in semis.
Goldman favors owning downside skew while Nomura's exotics flow leans against negative spot-vol, describing different books.
